checks: If W_i=0 then the nonnegative cap measure α_0 μ_i has zero mass. Since (L_i)_+ vanishes off the closed cap, α_0 Ψ_i=0.

For W_i>0 both normalized positive measure means lie in the compact convex body C. The base first-moment equality and common normalization give identical real base coordinates, so the continuous-coordinate difference is in D_all by its defining slice.

Affineness of L_i turns the pairing of that difference with u_i into the difference of the two mean margins. The section and contact means have zero margin, leaving exactly α_0 Ψ_i/W_i. The sign is positive and h_{D_all}(u_i)=1 bounds it above.
Summing over i at α_0=1 gives the total quotient because all representatives have denominator one, and ∑_i λ_{zi}=1 yields ∑_i W_i=∑_z η_z. The term r_iS_i remains in each row.

The original §4 explicitly derives the same weaker-premise version without the continuous vector moment identity. The proof establishes the bound conditional on the measures and does not assert their existence at a general minimizer.
